doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Coltrane, Jimmy Smith and musical values
title: Donald Bailey and the drummers he has worked with
summary: Burrell praises Donald Bailey, lists drummers, and recalls Sherman Ferguson.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And Jimmy had been working with Donald Bailey for a long time.
Oh, I love Donald Bailey. Donald Bailey, I love him, another underrated musician.
He’s up in the Bay area…
Yeah, I know, I know. Brown:…so we just had a tribute for him.
I know, that’s one of my favorite musicians, man.
Well, what is it about the drummers? I mean, yes, you’ve worked with all the piano players, you played with all the great leaders. But you’ve also played with all the great drummers…
I certainly have. Brown:…I mean, your first recording is with Elvin. You know, and we can bring in everybody.
Philly Joe, Papa Jo - you name it - Shelly Manne, you name it.
So what is it, when you, the last time we saw you perform live was at the IAJE when you had Sherman Ferguson, rest in peace…

My man, yeah. Brown:…so, I mean, the breadth of the different styles you seem to be able to, not only function, but to create some sort of synergistic effect. I mean, watching you with Sherman was a real treat.
You know, that was tremendous, you know…
So what is it you look for in a drummer? What is it that you want a drummer to provide? I know there are so many different contexts, but is there a general or…
